questions.question: Name four kinds of energy around us and give an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Movement energy, for example a rushing river or a moving car. Heat energy, for example a campfire or the Sun. Light energy, for example a torch or the Sun. Sound energy, for example a guitar or a croaking frog.

questions.question: Name five stores of energy.
questions.expected_answer: Food, wood, coal, oil products such as petrol, diesel and paraffin, and natural gas.

questions.question: What happens to the energy stored in wood when it burns, and why can we not burn the same wood again?
questions.expected_answer: When wood burns, its stored energy is released as heat and light. The wood turns into ash and smoke, and its stored energy is used up, so it cannot burn again.
